newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Subversion trials of 10 Indonesian activists open.
newsitem.headline: Subversion trials of 10 Indonesian activists open.

text.p: Trials began on Thursday for 10 Indonesian activists, including independent labour leader Muchtar Pakpahan, on charges of subversion.
Defence lawyers said they were pessimistic about the outcome. Subversion carries the death penalty in Indonesia.

Pakpahan, head of the Indonesian Labour Welfare Union (SBSI), was accused in the South Jakarta State Court of subversion and spreading hatred against the government in a book and other statements between August 1995 and July 27, 1996.

The prosecutor claimed Pakpahan made a number of subversive and anti-government statements, including that he would use a "people's power revolution" if he could not achieve reform through constitutional means.
The indictment said the subversive remarks were also made during a speech at a Portuguese university in February and during an interview with Dutch television in July this year at his home.
Nine activists from the left-wing People's Democratic Party (PRD) faced similiar charges in five separate but simultaneous trials.

"Muchtar Pakpahan made attacks with the intention or effect, which he knew or should have known, could overturn, damage or undermine the state's authority, the authority of the legal government or the state apparatus," prosecutor R. Moekiat said.

The PRD activists, including their leader Budiman Sudjatmiko, are accused of founding a group which was not based on the state ideology, supported higher minimum wages as well as a referendum for East Timor.
The PRD was also singled out for its call for an end to the involvement of the Indonesian military in social and political affairs under its long-standing dual function doctrine.
All the accused were picked up in a government crackdown in the wake of Jakarta's July 27 riots, the worst in 20 years in the capital in which at least five people died.
Indonesia's military said on Wednesday the group of leftwing activists was being prosecuted for their political manifesto rather than links to Jakarta's riots.

One of Pakpahan's defence lawyers, high-profile human rights advocate Adnan Buyung Nasution, said after the 90-minute hearing the defence team felt there was only a slim chance of Pakpahan being acquitted.
"I think it will be a very tough trial," Nasution said, after lawyers clashed on a number of occasions with head judge Djazuli Sudibyo in the Pakpahan case over minor legal technicalities.

Sudjatmiko's indictment indicated that similar charges would soon be made against three PRD leaders due to go on trial in Surabaya, East Java on Monday and three other PRD members awaiting trial in Semarang, Central Java.
Witnesses said the other cases proceeded without incident amid tight security with dozens of riot police in attendance at both court houses.
